question: What does reproductive health cover according to standard health definitions?

options.A: Only the ability to bear children without medical complications
options.B: The prevention of sexually transmitted diseases in teenagers
options.C: The total absence of any infection in the pelvic organs
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health is a broad state of complete well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity in reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is the nurse considered a vital link in community reproductive health?

options.A: Nurses perform all surgical procedures related to reproductive organs
options.B: Nurses have the sole authority to distribute contraceptive drugs
options.C: Nurses connect community members to formal health institutions and provide primary care
options.D: Nurses write the national policies governing family planning services

explanation: Nurses work directly within communities and clinics, making them the primary bridge for education, prevention, and basic care delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.A: To treat infertility using modern assisted reproductive technology
options.B: To cure advanced stages of reproductive tract cancers
options.C: To stop health problems before they start through screening and education
options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept diseases early or stop them entirely using vaccines, screenings, and education. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of family planning counseling?

options.A: To eliminate population growth in developing nations completely
options.B: To force every woman of childbearing age to use hormonal contraception
options.C: To promote permanent surgical sterilization for all young couples
options.D: To help clients make informed choices about child spacing and family size

explanation: Family planning empowers clients with information to choose their preferred method safely and voluntarily. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: A client expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive will cause permanent infertility. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Agree that hormonal drugs permanently damage the womb and suggest avoiding them
options.B: Insist she takes the injection anyway because healthcare workers know best
options.C: Explain that fertility generally returns after the drug wears off, though it may take a few months
options.D: Tell the client that her fears are unfounded and scold her for listening to myths

explanation: Nurses must address client fears respectfully with accurate medical facts rather than dismissing or forcing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main tool used by nurses during labor to track progress and detect complications early?
explanation: The partograph is a graphic record of labor used to monitor maternal and fetal well-being and flag prolonged labor. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: A woman who delivered a healthy baby six hours ago starts bleeding heavily, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.B: Leave the ward to call the senior consultant doctor immediately
options.C: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.D: Massage the uterus gently to stimulate contraction and expel clots

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus after delivery indicates uterine atony, which requires immediate fundal massage to stimulate contraction and reduce bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Treating infections based on recognized groups of symptoms when lab tests are unavailable
options.B: Isolating infected patients in private hospital wards for weeks
options.C: Waiting for definitive blood culture results before starting any medication
options.D: Treating only the male partner in cases of recurrent vaginal discharge

explanation: Syndromic management allows prompt treatment of common STI symptoms during the initial clinic visit using standardized flowcharts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is partner notification and treatment critical when managing a patient with an STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission in the community
options.B: To ensure the hospital can collect double consultation fees from both clients
options.C: To punish the partner for bringing the infection into the relationship
options.D: To force both individuals to undergo permanent surgical sterilization

explanation: Treating only one partner leads to rapid reinfection when sexual contact resumes, making joint treatment necessary. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which feature is most essential for a successful adolescent reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Charging high fees to discourage casual visits by teenagers
options.B: Youth-friendly services with strict privacy and non-judgmental staff
options.C: Mandatory reporting of all adolescent clinic visitors to their parents
options.D: Locating the clinic inside high school classrooms during lessons

explanation: Adolescents avoid health facilities if they fear moral judgment or lack of confidentiality from staff. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.A: Adolescents immediately change their behavior and practice strict abstinence
options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes drive vulnerable youths away from clinics, leading to hidden risks like unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What does informed consent require before a nurse or doctor performs a reproductive health procedure?

options.A: The hospital management approves the procedure during a board meeting
options.B: The client understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The head of the family gives written permission on behalf of the client
options.D: The local community leader signs a clearance certificate

explanation: Informed consent is an ethical requirement ensuring the patient is fully aware and willing without coercion. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following actions represents a breach of nursing ethics in reproductive health?

options.A: Discussing a patient's private HIV test result with coworkers in the cafeteria
options.B: Providing confidential contraceptive counseling to an unmarried adult woman
options.C: Reporting a case of child abuse to the appropriate hospital social worker
options.D: Refusing to perform female genital mutilation because it is harmful

explanation: Sharing private patient information outside the direct care team violates confidentiality and patient rights. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)
